Wisconsin State Trooper dies after fall from I-94 bridge

By Nolan Kopydlowski
Published: Oct. 3, 2026 at 10:17 AM EDT
Add Us On GoogleAdd as a preferred source on Google
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 2:17
Instaread

ELK MOUND, Wis. (WMTV) - A Wisconsin State Patrol Trooper has died nearly two weeks after falling from a bridge on I-94 in Elk Mound, according to officials.

In a Facebook post, the Wisconsin State Patrol and the Wisconsin Department of Transportation said Trooper Bradley Ritger died in the line-of-duty at the age of 29.

Authorities said Trooper Ritger was called to a traffic pursuit on I-94, just before 5 a.m. on September 21.

According to state patrol, Trooper Ritger deployed a tire deflation device on a bridge deck west of the Dunn County/Eau Claire County line. He went to move to a position of cover, before falling several feet from the bridge onto the road below.

Trooper Ritger was severely hurt from the fall, with life-saving measures including CPR administered on scene. He was later taken to a nearby medical facility.

Despite life-saving efforts and critical medical care, officials said Trooper Ritger died from his injuries on Friday, October 2.

In their post, authorities shared more about who Trooper Ritger was. He joined the Wisconsin State Patrol as a member of the 67th Recruit Class, and served in the northwest region around Dunn County for nearly five years.

Trooper Ritger also gained certifications as a general law enforcement instructor, mobile field force team member and squad leader, and salvage vehicle inspector.

Before serving with the Wisconsin State Patrol, Trooper Ritger also served with the Wisconsin Department of Corrections for three years.

10/3/26 - Wisconsin State Patrol Statement

Trooper Ritger was a dedicated public servant whose strong work ethic and positive presence left a lasting impact on anyone who had the privilege of knowing him. He approached every situation with professionalism, integrity and a genuine commitment to serving others. Whether assisting the public, supporting his fellow troopers, or taking on difficult challenges, he consistently demonstrated compassion and willingness to help wherever needed. His dedication to his family and unwavering commitment to his profession will not be forgotten.

We extend our deepest sympathy to Trooper Ritger’s family, friends, loved ones and all who served alongside him. As the community mourns, the Wisconsin State Patrol has placed a law enforcement memorial vehicle at its Northwest Region Post in Eau Claire where the public is welcome to drop off cards, flowers, or other condolences.

Wisconsin State Patrol

Governor Tony Evers released a statement Saturday, saying he is praying for Trooper Ritger’s loved ones and those who worked with him.

“Our hearts break for Trooper Ritger and his family,” Evers said. “He was already leading a life of public service and dedication to our state, and our state workers join his coworkers and colleagues, friends, and loved ones in mourning his passing. This was a young life lost far too soon.”

WisDOT officials said out of respect for Trooper Ritger’s family, no additional information will be shared right now. Funeral arrangements are being made by the family.

Wisconsin State Patrol asked the public to respect the family’s privacy while they grieve this tragedy.
